entries.passageText: Who have believed and whose hearts have rest in the remembrance of Allah. Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!
entries.reflection: Hearts are restless by nature, pulled by worry and noise. This verse names where rest is found: in the remembrance of Allah. Even a brief remembrance between tasks can return the heart to calm.
studyPrompts: What is unsettling your heart most today?
When during your day could you pause for remembrance?
How have you experienced calm through prayer or dhikr before?

entries.passageText: He said: Fear not. Lo! I am with you twain, Hearing and Seeing.
entries.reflection: Moses and Aaron were sent on a daunting mission and admitted their fear. Allah's answer was not that the task was easy, but that He was with them, hearing and seeing. Courage grows from knowing you are not unseen.
studyPrompts: What task in front of you feels daunting?
How does knowing Allah hears and sees change how you approach it?
Who could you support as they face something difficult?

entries.passageText: And will provide for him from (a quarter) whence he hath no expectation. And whosoever putteth his trust in Allah, He will suffice him. Lo! Allah bringeth His command to pass. Allah hath set a measure for all things.
entries.reflection: Worry often comes from trying to carry every outcome ourselves. This verse reminds the believer that provision can come from where we least expect, and that Allah suffices whoever puts their trust in Him. Do your part, then let the weight of the outcome rest with Him.
studyPrompts: Which outcome are you trying hardest to control right now?
What does putting your trust in Allah look like alongside doing your duty well?
When has help come to you from an unexpected place?

entries.passageText: And have appointed your sleep for repose, And have appointed the night as a cloak, And have appointed the day for livelihood.
entries.reflection: Sleep, night, and day are named here as gifts, each with its purpose. Rest is part of the design, not a weakness. When duty allows, receive sleep as a mercy rather than time lost.
studyPrompts: How are you sleeping and resting lately?
What keeps you from receiving rest as a gift?
How could you better balance work and rest this week?

entries.passageText: Therefore remember Me, I will remember you. Give thanks to Me, and reject not Me.
entries.reflection: Remembrance and gratitude are tied together here: remember Allah and He remembers you; give thanks and do not be ungrateful. Gratitude keeps blessings in view when circumstances are hard. Today, name a few blessings you might otherwise overlook.
studyPrompts: What blessings have you overlooked recently?
How does being remembered by Allah encourage you?
How could you express thanks to the people around you today?

entries.passageText: But lo! with hardship goeth ease, Lo! with hardship goeth ease;
entries.reflection: The promise is repeated so that it is not missed: with hardship goes ease. Ease does not only come after hardship; it comes with it. Look for the small ease within today's difficulty.
studyPrompts: What hardship are you facing right now?
What ease, however small, can you find within it?
Why do you think this promise is repeated?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Seek help in steadfastness and prayer. Lo! Allah is with the steadfast.
entries.reflection: Steadfastness and prayer are offered as the two supports for hard times. Allah is with the steadfast, so patience is never endured alone. Keeping prayer even in a demanding schedule is itself an act of steadfastness.
studyPrompts: Where do you most need steadfastness right now?
How does prayer help you carry what is hard?
What would help you keep your prayers during a busy or irregular schedule?

entries.passageText: And verily whoso is patient and forgiveth - lo! that, verily, is (of) the steadfast heart of things.
entries.reflection: Patience and forgiveness are described here as the steadfast heart of things, not as weakness. In close quarters, small wrongs happen often. Choosing to forgive is a strength that keeps a unit, and a heart, intact.
studyPrompts: Is there someone you find it hard to forgive right now?
How is forgiveness a form of strength?
What would patience look like in a relationship that tests you?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Be ye staunch in justice, witnesses for Allah, even though it be against yourselves or (your) parents or (your) kindred, whether (the case be of) a rich man or a poor man, for Allah is nearer unto both (them ye are). So follow not passion lest ye lapse (from truth) and if ye lapse or fall away, then lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do.
entries.reflection: This verse asks for justice even when it costs us or those we love. Integrity means the truth does not change depending on who benefits. It names personal desire as the thing that pulls us away from fairness.
studyPrompts: Where are you tempted to bend the truth for yourself or someone close to you?
What helps you stay fair when your own interests are involved?
What does it mean to be a witness for Allah in your daily work?

entries.passageText: And when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh. I answer the prayer of the suppliant when he crieth unto Me. So let them hear My call and let them trust in Me, in order that they may be led aright.
entries.reflection: Allah answers the question before it is fully asked: I am near. No distance from home, family, or community puts a believer out of reach of His hearing. Call on Him from wherever you are tonight.
studyPrompts: When do you feel most alone?
What would you like to say to Allah tonight?
How can you stay connected to your faith community while far from home?

entries.passageText: And surely We shall try you with something of fear and hunger, and loss of wealth and lives and crops; but give glad tidings to the steadfast, Who say, when a misfortune striketh them: Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning.
entries.reflection: The Qur'an names loss of lives among the trials of this world and gives the steadfast a phrase for it: we belong to Allah and to Him we return. Many Muslims say these words on hearing of a death. They hold grief within a larger trust.
studyPrompts: What loss are you carrying right now?
What does it mean to you that we belong to Allah?
Who could you share your grief with?

entries.passageText: Lo! Allah commandeth you that ye restore deposits to their owners, and, if ye judge between mankind, that ye judge justly. Lo! comely is this which Allah admonisheth you. Lo! Allah is ever Hearer, Seer.
entries.reflection: This verse commands returning trusts to their owners and judging justly. Duty includes the things placed in your care: equipment, information, people. Keeping a trust well is an act of faith.
studyPrompts: What has been entrusted to your care?
How do you keep trusts when no one is checking?
Where do you need to act more justly?

entries.passageText: He said: I expose my distress and anguish only unto Allah, and I know from Allah that which ye know not.
entries.reflection: Jacob, separated from his son Joseph for years, takes his sorrow to Allah alone, while holding to what he knows of Allah. Separation from family is a real pain. Like Jacob, you can bring it honestly to Allah without losing hope.
studyPrompts: Who are you separated from right now?
What sorrow do you need to bring to Allah?
What helps you hold on to hope during separation?

entries.passageText: The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace;
entries.reflection: The servants of the Beneficent walk on the earth modestly and answer the foolish with peace. Humility shows in how we carry ourselves and how we respond to provocation. It is a quiet strength.
studyPrompts: How do you carry yourself among others?
How do you respond when someone is rude or foolish?
Who models humility for you?

entries.passageText: By the declining day, Lo! man is a state of loss, Save those who believe and do good works, and exhort one another to truth and exhort one another to endurance.
entries.reflection: Surah al-Asr says people are in loss except those who believe, do good, and urge one another to truth and to endurance. Patience is not only personal; we encourage it in each other. Endurance is a shared effort.
studyPrompts: Who encourages you to endure?
Who could you encourage today?
What helps you stay patient in hard times?

entries.passageText: A kind word with forgiveness is better than almsgiving followed by injury. Allah is Absolute, Clement.
entries.reflection: A kind word with forgiveness is better than charity that is followed by hurt. Kindness is not only giving things; it is how we treat people. Words can heal or wound.
studyPrompts: What kind word could you offer today?
When has a kind word stayed with you?
Have you ever given help in a way that hurt?

entries.passageText: Who hath created life and death that He may try you which of you is best in conduct; and He is the Mighty, the Forgiving,
entries.reflection: Allah created life and death to test which of us is best in conduct. Purpose, in this verse, is about how we live, not what we achieve. Every day is a chance to do good.
studyPrompts: What does being best in conduct mean to you?
How does seeing life as a test change your choices?
What good deed can you do today?

entries.passageText: Lo! He Who hath given thee the Qur'an for a law will surely bring thee home again. Say: My Lord is Best Aware of him who bringeth guidance and him who is in error manifest.
entries.reflection: Many commentators read this verse as Allah's promise to the Prophet that he would return home to Mecca. It speaks to everyone who is far from home and longs to return. The One who sent you out can bring you back.
studyPrompts: What do you miss most about home?
What are you looking forward to on your return?
How can you keep faith while you wait?

entries.passageText: Those who spend (of that which Allah hath given them) in ease and in adversity, those who control their wrath and are forgiving toward mankind; Allah loveth the good;
entries.reflection: Among the qualities of the righteous are controlling anger and forgiving people. Anger may arise, but the believer holds it back. That restraint is loved by Allah.
studyPrompts: What has made you angry recently?
What helps you control your anger?
Who do you need to forgive?

entries.passageText: And put thy trust in Allah, for Allah is sufficient as Trustee.
entries.reflection: Put your trust in Allah; He is enough as a Trustee. Tawakkul does not mean doing nothing; it means doing your part and leaving the outcome with Him. It lifts a weight you were not meant to carry.
studyPrompts: What outcome are you trying hardest to control?
What is your part, and what is Allah's?
How does trusting Allah bring you peace?

entries.passageText: The believers are naught else than brothers. Therefore make peace between your brethren and observe your duty to Allah that haply ye may obtain mercy.
entries.reflection: The believers are brothers, so make peace between them. Brotherhood in faith brings duties: to reconcile, to support, to keep peace. A unit can be like this too.
studyPrompts: Is there a conflict between people near you that you could help resolve?
Who do you consider a brother or sister in faith?
How can you strengthen bonds in your unit?

entries.passageText: But as for him who feared to stand before his Lord and restrained his soul from lust, Lo! the Garden will be his home.
entries.reflection: This verse speaks of the one who restrained the soul from its desires out of awe of standing before Allah. Self-control is shaped by remembering Allah. Small acts of restraint build that habit.
studyPrompts: What desire do you most need to restrain?
How does remembering Allah help you hold back?
What small act of self-control can you practise today?

entries.passageText: And strain not thine eyes toward that which We cause some wedded pairs among them to enjoy, the flower of the life of the world, that We may try them thereby. The provision of thy Lord is better and more lasting.
entries.reflection: Do not strain your eyes toward what others have been given to enjoy, for the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. Comparison breeds discontent. Contentment comes from looking at what Allah has given you.
studyPrompts: Whose life do you find yourself comparing to your own?
What provision from Allah are you grateful for?
What lasts longer than what you are tempted to envy?

entries.passageText: Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
entries.reflection: Despair not of the mercy of Allah, who forgives all sins. This verse is offered to those who feel they have gone too far. No one is beyond His mercy.
studyPrompts: Is there something you feel cannot be forgiven?
How does this verse speak to you?
How can you show mercy to others as you have received it?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Guard your duty to Allah, and speak words straight to the point; He will adjust your works for you and will forgive you your sins. Whosoever obeyeth Allah and His messenger, he verily hath gained a signal victory.
entries.reflection: Believers are asked to speak words that are straight, direct and true. Honest speech is tied to having one's deeds set right. Truthfulness is part of taqwa.
studyPrompts: Is there something you need to say plainly?
When is honesty hardest for you?
How has honesty helped you or others?

entries.passageText: And with Him are the keys of the Invisible. None but He knoweth them. And He knoweth what is in the land and the sea. Not a leaf falleth but He knoweth it, not a grain amid the darkness of the earth, naught of wet or dry but (it is noted) in a clear record.
entries.reflection: The keys of the unseen are with Allah alone; not a leaf falls without His knowledge. When the future is unclear, this reminds you that nothing is hidden from Him. You do not have to know everything.
studyPrompts: What is uncertain for you right now?
How does knowing Allah sees all affect your worry?
What can you leave in His hands?

entries.passageText: The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah's way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah giveth increase manifold to whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing.
entries.reflection: Spending in Allah's way is like a seed that grows into seven ears with a hundred grains each. Generosity multiplies beyond what we give. Even small giving bears fruit.
studyPrompts: What could you give this week?
When have you seen a small kindness grow?
What holds you back from giving?

entries.passageText: It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah. Lo! Allah loveth those who put their trust (in Him).
entries.reflection: This verse tells the Prophet that it was by Allah's mercy that he was gentle with people, and that harshness would have driven them away. It then tells him to pardon, to consult, and then to decide and trust Allah. That is a model of leadership: gentle, consultative and decisive.
studyPrompts: How do you consult others before deciding?
Where could you lead more gently?
How do you balance consultation and decision?

entries.passageText: And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him, (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks from you;
entries.reflection: The righteous feed the needy, the orphan and the captive, wanting no reward or thanks, only Allah's pleasure. Service without seeking credit is pure. It frees you from needing recognition.
studyPrompts: Who could you serve this week without being noticed?
Do you look for thanks when you help?
What does serving for Allah's sake mean to you?

entries.passageText: He giveth wisdom unto whom He will, and he unto whom wisdom is given, he truly hath received abundant good. But none remember except men of understanding.
entries.reflection: Whoever is given wisdom has been given much good. Wisdom is a gift from Allah, and those of understanding take heed. Ask for it, and learn from those who have it.
studyPrompts: What decision needs wisdom from you now?
Who do you turn to for wise counsel?
How do you ask Allah for wisdom?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Be steadfast witnesses for Allah in equity, and let not hatred of any people seduce you that ye deal not justly. Deal justly, that is nearer to your duty. Observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do.
entries.reflection: Do not let hatred of any people lead you to be unjust. Be just, for that is nearer to piety. This is a demanding standard, especially in conflict: justice applies even to those you dislike.
studyPrompts: Is there someone you find it hard to treat fairly?
How does this verse challenge you?
What fair action can you take today?

entries.passageText: Every soul will taste of death. And ye will be paid on the Day of Resurrection only that which ye have fairly earned. Whoso is removed from the Fire and is made to enter paradise, he indeed is triumphant. The life of this world is but comfort of illusion.
entries.reflection: Every soul will taste death. The verse also says the life of this world is the comfort of illusion, and true success is beyond it. Remembering death puts daily concerns in proportion.
studyPrompts: How do you feel when you think about death?
What matters most in light of it?
What would you want to have done before you meet Allah?

entries.passageText: Know that Allah quickeneth the earth after its death. We have made clear Our revelations for you, that haply ye may understand.
entries.reflection: Allah gives life to the earth after its death. Rain on dry ground is a sign of renewal. Hearts can be revived in the same way.
studyPrompts: Where do you feel dry or worn out?
What revives your heart?
How have you seen renewal in your life before?

entries.passageText: And do thou (O Muhammad) remember thy Lord within thyself humbly and with awe, below thy breath, at morn and evening. And be not thou of the neglectful.
entries.reflection: Remember your Lord within yourself, humbly, quietly, morning and evening. Dhikr does not need to be loud. Stillness and remembrance go together.
studyPrompts: When could you remember Allah quietly today?
What helps you find stillness?
How does quiet remembrance affect you?

entries.passageText: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and afterward are upright, the angels descend upon them, saying: Fear not nor grieve, but hear good tidings of the paradise which ye are promised.
entries.reflection: Those who say our Lord is Allah and then stay upright receive the angels' message: do not fear, do not grieve. Steadfastness is staying upright after the first commitment. It brings peace.
studyPrompts: What commitment do you need to stay steady in?
What makes steadfastness hard?
How have you seen Allah strengthen your resolve?

entries.passageText: Therefor the orphan oppress not, Therefor the beggar drive not away,
entries.reflection: Do not oppress the orphan, and do not turn away the one who asks. These verses come after Allah reminds the Prophet of his own care when he was an orphan. Compassion grows from remembering what we were given.
studyPrompts: When were you cared for when you needed it?
Who around you is vulnerable?
How can you show compassion today?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Observe your duty to Allah. And let every soul look to that which it sendeth on before for the morrow. And observe your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Informed of what ye do.
entries.reflection: Let every soul look to what it has sent ahead for tomorrow. Reflection here means considering your deeds in light of the Hereafter. It is honest self-accounting.
studyPrompts: What have you sent ahead today?
What would you change if you looked at your deeds honestly?
When do you set aside time for self-accounting?

entries.passageText: Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy: therein let them rejoice. It is better than what they hoard.
entries.reflection: Rejoice in Allah's bounty and mercy, which are better than whatever people hoard. Real joy comes from gifts that cannot be stored or lost. It is available even when other things are scarce.
studyPrompts: What bounty from Allah can you rejoice in today?
What do you hoard that cannot bring you joy?
How can you share joy with others?

entries.passageText: Every soul is a pledge for its own deeds;
entries.reflection: Every soul is a pledge for its own deeds. We are responsible for our own deeds. No one else can carry that for us, and no one else can take it away.
studyPrompts: What deeds are you responsible for today?
How do you take ownership of your mistakes?
What does this verse ask of you?

entries.passageText: Everyone that is thereon will pass away; There remaineth but the Countenance of thy Lord of Might and Glory.
entries.reflection: All that is on the earth will pass away; only the Face of your Lord remains. Service life is full of change. These verses point to the one thing that never changes.
studyPrompts: What change are you facing right now?
What gives you stability in change?
How does Allah's permanence comfort you?

entries.passageText: Appoint for me a henchman from my folk, Aaron, my brother. Confirm my strength with him And let him share my task,
entries.reflection: Moses asks Allah to give him a helper, his brother Aaron, to strengthen him and share his task. Even a prophet asked for help. There is no shame in needing others.
studyPrompts: What task do you need help with?
Who could be an Aaron for you?
Who might need you to be an Aaron for them?

entries.passageText: And who are shepherds of their pledge and their covenant,
entries.reflection: The believers are those who keep their trusts and their covenants. Loyalty means keeping your word. In service, promises to comrades and commitments made carry weight.
studyPrompts: What promises have you made that you need to keep?
Who relies on your word?
What makes keeping your word hard?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, even as it was prescribed for those before you, that ye may ward off (evil);
entries.reflection: Fasting is prescribed so that you may attain taqwa. Discipline of the body serves growth of the soul. Training in one area strengthens the whole person.
studyPrompts: What discipline helps you grow?
How has fasting or self-denial affected you?
What habit could you build this week?

entries.passageText: Who hear advice and follow the best thereof. Such are those whom Allah guideth, and such are men of understanding.
entries.reflection: Those who listen to what is said and follow the best of it are guided. Listening well means taking in what you hear and choosing the best. It is a mark of understanding.
studyPrompts: Who do you need to listen to more carefully?
How do you choose what advice to follow?
What gets in the way of listening?

entries.passageText: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend.
entries.reflection: Repel evil with what is better, and an enemy may become a close friend. Gentleness can transform a relationship. It takes strength to answer harm with good.
studyPrompts: Is there someone you are in conflict with?
What would answering with good look like?
When has gentleness changed a situation?

entries.passageText: Allah is He Who shaped you out of weakness, then appointed after weakness strength, then, after strength, appointed weakness and grey hair. He createth what He will. He is the Knower, the Mighty.
entries.reflection: Allah created us in weakness, then gave strength, then weakness again in old age. Strength is a stage and a trust, not a permanent possession. Use it well while you have it.
studyPrompts: How are you using the strength you have now?
How do you face your own weakness?
Who needs your strength right now?

entries.passageText: And the believers, men and women, are protecting friends one of another; they enjoin the right and forbid the wrong, and they establish worship and they pay the poor-due, and they obey Allah and His messenger. As for these, Allah will have mercy on them. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise.
entries.reflection: The believers, men and women, are protecting friends of one another. They encourage right, discourage wrong, and support each other in faith. Friendship has a purpose.
studyPrompts: Who are your protecting friends?
How do you help each other do right?
How could you be a better friend?

entries.passageText: (And when they came unto their father and had spoken thus to him) he said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience! It may be that Allah will bring them all unto me. Lo! He, only He, is the Knower, the Wise.
entries.reflection: When Jacob lost another son, he answered with comely patience and hope that Allah would bring them all back to him. Waiting with patience is not giving up. It is holding on to hope.
studyPrompts: What are you waiting on?
What would comely patience look like for you?
What gives you hope while you wait?

entries.passageText: Seest thou not how Allah coineth a similitude: A goodly saying, as a goodly tree, its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven, Giving its fruit at every season by permission of its Lord? Allah coineth the similitudes for mankind in order that they may reflect.
entries.reflection: A goodly saying is like a goodly tree, its root set firm and its branches reaching into heaven, giving fruit in every season. Good words keep giving. Choose them carefully.
studyPrompts: What good word has borne fruit in your life?
What words do you want to plant?
What words do you want to stop saying?

entries.passageText: And we task not any soul beyond its scope, and with Us is a Record which speaketh the truth, and they will not be wronged.
entries.reflection: Allah does not task any soul beyond its scope. When you feel stretched, this verse is a reminder that the load is measured. Rest and ask for help when you need it.
studyPrompts: Where do you feel stretched?
What would it mean to trust that your load is measured?
What help do you need?

entries.passageText: Establish worship at the two ends of the day and in some watches of the night. Lo! good deeds annul ill-deeds. This is reminder for the mindful.
entries.reflection: Good deeds annul ill deeds. This verse speaks of prayer at the ends of the day and in the night. Every prayer and good act is a chance to begin again.
studyPrompts: What would you like to begin again?
What good deed could you do today?
How do your daily prayers help you reset?

entries.passageText: And those who, when they spend, are neither prodigal nor grudging; and there is ever a firm station between the two;
entries.reflection: The Qur'an describes the faithful servants of the Beneficent as people who spend neither wastefully nor stingily, but keep a balance between the two. Simplicity is moderation. The middle way is a strong place to stand.
studyPrompts: Where do you tend toward excess?
Where do you tend to hold back too much?
What would balance look like for you?

entries.passageText: And that man hath only that for which he maketh effort, And that his effort will be seen.
entries.reflection: A person has only what they strive for, and their effort will be seen. Effort matters. Nothing sincere is wasted.
studyPrompts: What are you striving for?
Is your effort going where you want it?
What effort of yours do you hope will be seen?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Let not a folk deride a folk who may be better than they (are), not let women (deride) women who may be better than they are; neither defame one another, nor insult one another by nicknames. Bad is the name of lewdness after faith. And whoso turneth not in repentance, such are evil-doers.
entries.reflection: The Qur'an forbids mocking others, insulting them, or calling them by offensive nicknames, since they may be better than you. Respect is a command. Banter in a unit can cross into contempt.
studyPrompts: When has teasing gone too far around you?
Who is easy to mock?
How could you protect someone's dignity today?

entries.passageText: By the morning hours And by the night when it is stillest, Thy Lord hath not forsaken thee nor doth He hate thee,
entries.reflection: By the morning hours and the still night, your Lord has not forsaken you. Many commentators link this surah to a pause in revelation, when the Prophet felt forsaken. Each morning carries that reassurance.
studyPrompts: Do you feel forgotten in any way?
What does a new morning mean to you?
How could you remind someone else they are not forsaken?

entries.passageText: And He it is Who maketh night a covering for you, and sleep repose, and maketh day a resurrection.
entries.reflection: Allah made the night a covering, sleep a rest, and the day a rising. Rhythm is a mercy. Night is given for rest.
studyPrompts: How well are you resting?
What keeps you from rest?
How could you honor the night as a gift?

entries.passageText: Who created me, and He doth guide me, And Who feedeth me and watereth me. And when I sicken, then He healeth me,
entries.reflection: Abraham says Allah created him, guides him, feeds him, and heals him when he is sick. Healing comes from Allah, often through doctors, care and time. Seeking treatment and trusting Him go together.
studyPrompts: What healing do you need?
Have you sought help for it?
Whom could you support in their healing?

entries.passageText: And those who, when they do an evil thing or wrong themselves, remember Allah and implore forgiveness for their sins - Who forgiveth sins save Allah only? - and will not knowingly repeat (the wrong) they did.
entries.reflection: Those who do wrong, then remember Allah, seek forgiveness and do not persist, are forgiven. Guilt can turn you back to Allah. The door of forgiveness is open.
studyPrompts: What wrong do you need to turn away from?
What stops you from seeking forgiveness?
What would not persisting look like?

entries.passageText: And to be of those who believe and exhort one another to perseverance and exhort one another to pity.
entries.reflection: The Ascent, the hard path this surah describes, includes being among those who believe and encourage one another to patience and compassion. Encouragement is part of faith. We help each other climb.
studyPrompts: Who encourages you to patience?
Whom could you encourage today?
What hard path are you climbing?

entries.passageText: And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate. And remember Allah's favour unto you: How ye were enemies and He made friendship between your hearts so that ye became as brothers by His grace; and (how) ye were upon the brink of an abyss of fire, and He did save you from it. Thus Allah maketh clear His revelations unto you, that haply ye may be guided,
entries.reflection: Hold fast, all together, to the cable of Allah and do not divide. The verse recalls how hearts once at war were joined as brothers. Unity is a blessing to remember and protect.
studyPrompts: What divides people around you?
What holds you together?
What could you do to protect unity?

entries.passageText: There is no good in much of their secret conferences save (in) him who enjoineth almsgiving and kindness and peace-making among the people. Whoso doeth that, seeking the good pleasure of Allah, We shall bestow on him a vast reward.
entries.reflection: There is little good in most private talk, except when it calls for charity, kindness or making peace between people. Peacemaking is among the best uses of speech.
studyPrompts: What do your private conversations usually focus on?
Where could you help make peace?
What kind word could you speak today?

entries.passageText: Hath the story of Abraham's honoured guests reached thee (O Muhammad)? When they came in unto him and said: Peace! he answered, Peace! (and thought): Folk unknown (to me). Then he went apart unto his housefolk so that they brought a fatted calf; And he set it before them, saying: Will ye not eat?
entries.reflection: Abraham greeted unknown guests with peace and quickly brought them a fine meal. His hospitality is an example. Welcome strangers generously.
studyPrompts: Who is a stranger around you?
How could you welcome them?
When has someone welcomed you generously?

entries.passageText: And lower unto them the wing of submission through mercy, and say: My Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little.
entries.reflection: Lower to your parents the wing of humility out of mercy, and pray for them as they cared for you when you were small. Kindness to parents is a duty. Distance does not cancel it.
studyPrompts: How do you show mercy to your parents?
What could you pray for them?
How could you reach out to family this week?

entries.passageText: And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect.
entries.reflection: Among Allah's signs is that He created helpmeets for you so that you may find rest in them, and placed love and mercy between you. Love and mercy are signs of Allah. Nurture them.
studyPrompts: Where do you find rest in your relationships?
How could you show love and mercy today?
What makes love hard when you are apart?

entries.passageText: And covet not the thing in which Allah hath made some of you excel others. Unto men a fortune from that which they have earned, and unto women a fortune from that which they have earned. (Envy not one another) but ask Allah of His bounty. Lo! Allah is ever Knower of all things.
entries.reflection: Do not covet what Allah has given others; ask Him of His bounty instead. Envy looks sideways. Gratitude and prayer look up.
studyPrompts: Whom are you tempted to envy?
What could you ask Allah for instead?
What are you grateful for?

entries.passageText: Say: Naught befalleth us save that which Allah hath decreed for us. He is our Protecting Friend. In Allah let believers put their trust!
entries.reflection: Nothing befalls us except what Allah has decreed. He is our protector, and in Him believers trust. Trust does not remove effort, but it can lighten worry.
studyPrompts: What worries you most today?
What is within your effort, and what must you trust?
How could you place your trust in Allah?

entries.passageText: Do men imagine that they will be left (at ease) because they say, We believe, and will not be tested with affliction?
entries.reflection: Do people think they will be left alone after saying we believe, without being tested? Hardship is part of a life of faith. It is not a sign you have been abandoned.
studyPrompts: What test are you facing?
How do you understand hardship?
Who supports you in it?

entries.passageText: I do not exculpate myself. Lo! the (human) soul enjoineth unto evil, save that whereon my Lord hath mercy. Lo! my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.
entries.reflection: The soul can urge toward evil, except when my Lord shows mercy. These words in Joseph's story (commentators differ on who speaks them) admit our weakness. Honesty about temptation is the first step to resisting it.
studyPrompts: What temptation do you face?
What helps you resist it?
How could you ask for mercy?

entries.passageText: There is no compulsion in religion. The right direction is henceforth distinct from error. And he who rejecteth false deities and believeth in Allah hath grasped a firm handhold which will never break. Allah is Hearer, Knower.
entries.reflection: There is no compulsion in religion. Faith must be freely chosen to be real. This verse also reminds us to respect the conscience of others.
studyPrompts: How freely do you hold your faith?
How do you respect others' beliefs?
What does freedom of conscience mean to you as someone who serves?

entries.passageText: Verily we have honoured the Children of Adam. We carry them on the land and the sea, and have made provision of good things for them, and have preferred them above many of those whom We created with a marked preferment.
entries.reflection: Allah has honored the children of Adam. Every person carries a dignity given by Allah. That is a reason to treat everyone with honor.
studyPrompts: How do you see the dignity of others?
Who do you struggle to honor?
How could you treat someone with honor today?

entries.passageText: Fulfil the covenant of Allah when ye have covenanted, and break not your oaths after the asseveration of them, and after ye have made Allah surety over you. Lo! Allah knoweth what ye do.
entries.reflection: Fulfill the covenant of Allah when you make it, and do not break oaths after confirming them. Keeping your word is a religious duty. Trust is built on it.
studyPrompts: What promise do you need to keep?
Do you make promises too easily?
Whose trust depends on your word?

entries.passageText: Whosoever doeth right, whether male or female, and is a believer, him verily we shall quicken with good life, and We shall pay them a recompense in proportion to the best of what they used to do.
entries.reflection: Whoever does good, male or female, while believing, will be given a good life. Good deeds are open to everyone. They shape the life you live.
studyPrompts: What good deed could you do today?
How do good deeds shape your life?
Whose good deeds inspire you?

entries.passageText: Ye will not attain unto piety until ye spend of that which ye love. And whatsoever ye spend, Allah is Aware thereof.
entries.reflection: You will not attain piety until you spend of that which you love. Giving what costs you something is true generosity. It may be time, attention or comfort.
studyPrompts: What do you love that you could share?
Whom could you give to?
What does it cost you to be generous?

entries.passageText: The steadfast, and the truthful, and the obedient, those who spend (and hoard not), those who pray for pardon in the watches of the night.
entries.reflection: The faithful are described as steadfast, truthful, obedient, generous, and praying for pardon in the watches of the night. Faithfulness is a cluster of steady habits. It is built over time.
studyPrompts: Which of these qualities is strongest in you?
Which needs attention?
What steady habit could you build?

entries.passageText: And a soul and Him Who perfected it And inspired it (with conscience of) what is wrong for it and (what is) right for it. He is indeed successful who causeth it to grow, And he is indeed a failure who stunteth it.
entries.reflection: Allah inspired the soul with knowledge of wrong and right; whoever purifies it succeeds, and whoever corrupts it fails. Character is shaped by daily choices.
studyPrompts: What is growing in your soul?
What is stunting it?
What choice today could help it grow?

entries.passageText: And He it is Who hath appointed night and day in succession, for him who desireth to remember, or desireth thankfulness.
entries.reflection: Allah made night and day follow each other for whoever wants to remember or to be grateful. The passing of time is an invitation. Each day is a chance to remember and to thank.
studyPrompts: How do you use the time you have?
What could you remember today?
What are you thankful for?

entries.passageText: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth, Createth man from a clot. Read: And thy Lord is the Most Bounteous, Who teacheth by the pen, Teacheth man that which he knew not.
entries.reflection: Read, in the name of your Lord, who taught by the pen, taught man what he did not know. The first revealed words call to learning. Knowledge is a gift from Allah.
studyPrompts: What are you learning right now?
How do you see learning as part of faith?
What do you want to know more about?

entries.passageText: Lo! In the creation of the heavens and the earth and (in) the difference of night and day are tokens (of His Sovereignty) for men of understanding,
entries.reflection: In the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for people of understanding. Creation is full of signs. Notice them.
studyPrompts: What sign have you noticed in creation lately?
How does creation lead you to reflect?
Where could you look up today?

entries.passageText: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is as it were a shining star. (This lamp is) kindled from a blessed tree, an olive neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil would almost glow forth (of itself) though no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guideth unto His light whom He will. And Allah speaketh to mankind in allegories, for Allah is Knower of all things.
entries.reflection: Allah is the light of the heavens and the earth, light upon light. This parable of the lamp is one of the Qur'an's most loved images. Divine light reaches even dark places.
studyPrompts: Where do you need light?
How does this image speak to you?
How could you carry light to others?

entries.passageText: Have We not caused thy bosom to dilate, And eased thee of the burden Which weighed down thy back;
entries.reflection: Did We not expand your chest and remove your burden that weighed on your back? These verses comforted the Prophet. They promise that heavy burdens can be lifted.
studyPrompts: What burden weighs on your back?
When has a burden been lifted before?
Whom could you help carry a load?

entries.passageText: Naught of disaster befalleth in the earth or in yourselves but it is in a Book before we bring it into being - Lo! that is easy for Allah - That ye grieve not for the sake of that which hath escaped you, nor yet exult because of that which hath been given. Allah loveth not all prideful boasters,
entries.reflection: Nothing happens except it is already known to Allah, so that you do not despair over what you missed or boast over what you gained. Perspective guards against both despair and pride.
studyPrompts: What loss are you grieving?
What gain might make you proud?
How does this verse change your view?

entries.passageText: And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then, And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then.
entries.reflection: Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. Small deeds count. Nothing is too small to matter.
studyPrompts: What small good could you do today?
What small wrong might you be ignoring?
Why do small things matter?

entries.passageText: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware.
entries.reflection: Allah made us nations and tribes so that we may know one another; the noblest is the one best in conduct. Diversity is meant for connection. Belonging is based on character, not origin.
studyPrompts: Who is different from you in your unit?
What could you learn from them?
How could you help someone belong?

entries.passageText: O my dear son! Establish worship and enjoin kindness and forbid iniquity, and persevere whatever may befall thee. Lo! that is of the steadfast heart of things.
entries.reflection: Luqman tells his son to establish worship, enjoin kindness, forbid iniquity, and persevere whatever may befall him. Standing for right takes courage and patience.
studyPrompts: Where do you need to stand for what is right?
What might befall you if you do?
What gives you courage?

entries.passageText: And serve Allah. Ascribe no thing as partner unto Him. (Show) kindness unto parents, and unto near kindred, and orphans, and the needy, and unto the neighbour who is of kin (unto you) and the neighbour who is not of kin, and the fellow-traveller and the wayfarer and (the slaves) whom your right hands possess. Lo! Allah loveth not such as are proud and boastful,
entries.reflection: Do good to parents, relatives, orphans, the needy, near and distant neighbors, companions and travelers. The circle of kindness is wide. Neighbors are part of it.
studyPrompts: Who are your neighbors right now?
Who is in your circle of kindness?
Whom could you add?

entries.passageText: O Children of Adam! Look to your adornment at every place of worship, and eat and drink, but be not prodigal. Lo! He loveth not the prodigals.
entries.reflection: Eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Moderation is a principle of health. Caring for your body is part of gratitude.
studyPrompts: How are your eating and drinking habits?
Where could you practice moderation?
How do you care for your health?

entries.passageText: Wealth and children are an ornament of the life of the world. But the good deeds which endure are better in thy Lord's sight for reward, and better in respect of hope.
entries.reflection: Wealth and children are adornments of this life, but lasting good deeds are better with Allah. Money is not the measure. What lasts is the good you do.
studyPrompts: How much does money shape your choices?
What good deeds will last?
What do you want to leave behind?

entries.passageText: And those who came (into the faith) after them say: Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord! Thou art Full of Pity, Merciful.
entries.reflection: Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who came before us in faith, and leave no rancor in our hearts. Praying for those who have gone keeps the bond alive.
studyPrompts: Whom do you remember in prayer?
What do you carry from those who came before?
Is there rancor you need to let go of?

entries.passageText: Moses said unto him: May I follow thee, to the end that thou mayst teach me right conduct of that which thou hast been taught?
entries.reflection: Moses asks to follow a wise teacher so he can learn right guidance. Even a prophet sought a teacher. Seeking mentors is a sign of wisdom, not weakness.
studyPrompts: Who mentors you?
What do you want to learn from them?
Whom could you mentor?

entries.passageText: So when thou art relieved, still toil And strive to please thy Lord.
entries.reflection: When you finish one task, strive on, and turn to your Lord. The end of one effort is the start of the next. Keep going with Allah in mind.
studyPrompts: What task are you finishing?
What comes next?
How will you turn to Allah on the road ahead?

entries.passageText: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the Worlds, The Beneficent, the Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment, Thee (alone) we worship; Thee (alone) we ask for help.
entries.reflection: The Qur'an opens with Al-Fatiha: in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. Many Muslims begin daily acts with Bismillah. Beginning in Allah's name gives a new start its direction.
studyPrompts: What are you beginning?
How does beginning with Bismillah change it?
What help would you ask for?

entries.passageText: The pilgrimage is (in) the well-known months, and whoever is minded to perform the pilgrimage therein (let him remember that) there is (to be) no lewdness nor abuse nor angry conversation on the pilgrimage. And whatsoever good ye do Allah knoweth it. So make provision for yourselves (Hereafter); for the best provision is to ward off evil. Therefore keep your duty unto Me, O men of understanding.
entries.reflection: In the verses on pilgrimage, the Qur'an says to take provision, and that the best provision is to ward off evil. Preparation is practical and spiritual.
studyPrompts: What are you preparing for?
What provision do you need?
What would spiritual preparation look like?

entries.passageText: He said: That wherein my Lord hath established me is better (than your tribute). Do but help me with strength (of men), I will set between you and them a bank.
entries.reflection: Dhu'l-Qarnayn turns down tribute and asks the people instead to help him with their strength, so together they can build a barrier. Shared labor builds what one person cannot.
studyPrompts: What could you build together with others?
What strength do you bring?
Where do you need others' help?

entries.passageText: And when Abraham said (unto his Lord): My Lord! Show me how Thou givest life to the dead, He said: Dost thou not believe? Abraham said: Yea, but (I ask) in order that my heart may be at ease. (His Lord) said: Take four of the birds and cause them to incline unto thee, then place a part of them on each hill, then call them, they will come to thee in haste, and know that Allah is Mighty, Wise.
entries.reflection: Abraham asked Allah to show him how He gives life to the dead, so that his heart might be at ease. Asking for reassurance is not lack of faith. Allah answered him.
studyPrompts: What question is on your heart?
What would put your heart at ease?
Who could you talk to about it?

entries.passageText: Who hath created seven heavens in harmony. Thou (Muhammad) canst see no fault in the Beneficent One's creation; then look again: Canst thou see any rifts? Then look again and yet again, thy sight will return unto thee weakened and made dim.
entries.reflection: Look again at the heavens, the Qur'an says: can you see any flaw? Look again and again. Wonder grows the more closely we look.
studyPrompts: What have you looked at closely lately?
Where do you see harmony?
How could you look again today?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Endure, outdo all others in endurance, be ready, and observe your duty to Allah, in order that ye may succeed.
entries.reflection: O you who believe, endure, outdo others in endurance, be ready, and keep your duty to Allah. Vigilance is steady readiness.
studyPrompts: What do you need to be ready for?
Where is your endurance tested?
What helps you stay ready?

entries.passageText: And who say: Our Lord! Vouchsafe us comfort of our wives and of our offspring, and make us patterns for (all) those who ward off (evil).
entries.reflection: The servants of the Beneficent pray for comfort in their spouses and children. Marriage is a source of comfort to pray for and protect.
studyPrompts: How could you pray for your spouse or loved one?
What brings comfort in your relationships?
How could you protect that bond from far away?

entries.passageText: Then they twain ate thereof, so that their shame became apparent unto them, and they began to hide by heaping on themselves some of the leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so went astray. Then his Lord chose him, and relented toward him, and guided him.
entries.reflection: Adam disobeyed and went astray, then his Lord chose him, turned to him in mercy and guided him. Failure was followed by return and guidance.
studyPrompts: What failure weighs on you?
What would turning back look like?
How have you been guided after a mistake?

entries.passageText: And that He it is who maketh laugh, and maketh weep,
entries.reflection: It is He who makes laugh and makes weep. Both laughter and tears come from Allah. Each has its time.
studyPrompts: When did you last laugh?
When did you last weep?
How do you hold both?

entries.passageText: (O man), follow not that whereof thou hast no knowledge. Lo! the hearing and the sight and the heart - of each of these it will be asked.
entries.reflection: Do not follow that of which you have no knowledge; the hearing, the sight and the heart will each be asked. Prudence means checking before acting.
studyPrompts: What are you assuming without knowing?
Where do you need more information?
How do you use your hearing, sight and heart well?

entries.passageText: O my bondmen who believe! Lo! My earth is spacious. Therefor serve Me only.
entries.reflection: Allah says My earth is spacious, so serve Me. Wherever you are, you can worship and belong. Distance from home does not mean distance from Allah.
studyPrompts: What do you miss about home?
How could you worship where you are?
What makes a place feel like home?

entries.passageText: The saying of (all true) believers when they appeal unto Allah and His messenger to judge between them is only that they say: We hear and we obey. And such are the successful.
entries.reflection: The believers say, we hear and we obey. Obedience to Allah is described as the mark of success.
studyPrompts: Where is it hard to obey?
What does hearing before obeying mean?
How could obedience bring peace?

entries.passageText: Who made all things good which He created, and He began the creation of man from clay;
entries.reflection: Allah made all things good which He created. Beauty is part of creation's design.
studyPrompts: What beauty have you noticed?
How does creation reflect its Maker?
Where could you look for beauty today?

entries.passageText: Yet whoso doeth evil or wrongeth his own soul, then seeketh pardon of Allah, will find Allah Forgiving, Merciful.
entries.reflection: Whoever does evil or wrongs their own soul, then seeks Allah's pardon, will find Him Forgiving, Merciful. Shame does not have to keep you away. The way back is open.
studyPrompts: What shame are you carrying?
What would seeking pardon look like?
Who could you talk to about it?

entries.passageText: Thy Lord hath decreed, that ye worship none save Him, and (that ye show) kindness to parents. If one of them or both of them attain old age with thee, say not "Fie" unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word.
entries.reflection: Allah has decreed kindness to parents. When they grow old, do not say even 'Fie' to them, but speak a gracious word. Kindness to parents is part of worship.
studyPrompts: How do you speak to your parents?
What gracious word could you give them?
What do they need from you now?

entries.passageText: Successful indeed are the believers Who are humble in their prayers,
entries.reflection: Successful indeed are the believers who are humble in their prayers. The Qur'an measures success by humility and devotion.
studyPrompts: How do you measure success?
How is your prayer life?
What would humble success look like?

entries.passageText: Lo! the vigil of the night is (a time) when impression is more keen and speech more certain.
entries.reflection: The vigil of the night is when impression is keenest and speech most certain. Night hours can be a time of deep prayer and clarity.
studyPrompts: What do you think about in the night?
How could night hours become prayer?
What becomes clear to you at night?

entries.passageText: Say: Lo! my worship and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds.
entries.reflection: My worship, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds. Sincerity means a life oriented toward Allah.
studyPrompts: What is your life oriented toward?
Where is your intention mixed?
How could you renew your intention today?

entries.passageText: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those of them with whom ye are at enmity. Allah is Mighty, and Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
entries.reflection: It may be that Allah will ordain love between you and those with whom you are at enmity. Enmity is not permanent. Hope for reconciliation.
studyPrompts: Who are you at odds with?
Could you hope for love between you?
What would a first step be?

entries.passageText: We have not revealed unto thee (Muhammad) this Qur'an that thou shouldst be distressed, But as a reminder unto him who feareth,
entries.reflection: Allah tells the Prophet the Qur'an was not revealed to cause him distress, but as a reminder. Faith is meant to ease, not to burden.
studyPrompts: What is causing you distress?
How could faith ease it?
What reminder do you need?

entries.passageText: And there is not a beast in the earth but the sustenance thereof dependeth on Allah. He knoweth its habitation and its repository. All is in a clear Record.
entries.reflection: There is no creature on earth whose provision is not with Allah. Daily provision comes from Him.
studyPrompts: What provision are you thankful for today?
Where do you worry about provision?
How could you trust Allah with it?

entries.passageText: My Lord! Make me to establish proper worship, and some of my posterity (also); our Lord! and accept my prayer.
entries.reflection: Abraham prayed that he and his descendants would establish prayer. Praying for one's children is a lasting gift.
studyPrompts: Which children could you pray for?
What do you hope for them?
How do you stay connected to them?

entries.passageText: And walk not in the earth exultant. Lo! thou canst not rend the earth, nor canst thou stretch to the height of the hills.
entries.reflection: Do not walk the earth exultantly; you cannot split the earth or reach the height of the mountains. Pride is put in perspective.
studyPrompts: Where are you tempted to boast?
What humbles you?
How could you walk more humbly today?

entries.passageText: When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it. Lo! Allah taketh count of all things.
entries.reflection: When you are greeted, return a better greeting or at least the same. Courtesy is a command.
studyPrompts: How do you greet people?
Whom could you greet more warmly?
What does a better greeting look like?

entries.passageText: And whosoever repenteth and doeth good, he verily repenteth toward Allah with true repentance -
entries.reflection: Whoever repents and does good truly turns to Allah. Regret becomes repentance when it leads to change.
studyPrompts: What do you regret?
What good could follow it?
What would true repentance look like?

entries.passageText: That ye may mount upon their backs, and may remember your Lord's favour when ye mount thereon, and may say: Glorified be He Who hath subdued these unto us, and we were not capable (of subduing them); And lo! unto our Lord we surely are returning.
entries.reflection: Muslims recite these words when setting out on a journey: glory to Him who has made this subservient to us, and to our Lord we are returning. Every journey begins with remembrance.
studyPrompts: Where is your journey taking you?
How could you begin it with remembrance?
What does returning to your Lord mean to you?

entries.passageText: Fill the measure when ye measure, and weigh with a right balance; that is meet, and better in the end.
entries.reflection: Give full measure and weigh with a right balance; that is better in the end. Fairness in dealings is a religious duty.
studyPrompts: Where might you cut corners?
What does full measure look like in your work?
How do you treat people fairly?

entries.passageText: And verily the latter portion will be better for thee than the former, And verily thy Lord will give unto thee so that thou wilt be content.
entries.reflection: The latter portion will be better for you than the former, and your Lord will give you so that you will be content. Discouragement is not the end of the story.
studyPrompts: What is discouraging you?
What might be better ahead?
Who could encourage you?

entries.passageText: He said: Have no fear this day! May Allah forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy.
entries.reflection: Joseph told the brothers who had wronged him: no blame on you this day; may Allah forgive you. Forgiving family can heal deep wounds.
studyPrompts: What is your relationship with your siblings like?
Is there forgiveness you could offer?
What would healing look like?

entries.passageText: Lo! as for those who believe and do good works - Lo! We suffer not the reward of one whose work is goodly to be lost.
entries.reflection: Allah does not let the reward of one whose work is goodly be lost. Excellent work is never wasted.
studyPrompts: What goodly work are you doing?
Where could you do better?
How does this promise encourage you?

entries.passageText: Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is in front of them and that which is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He will. His throne includeth the heavens and the earth, and He is never weary of preserving them. He is the Sublime, the Tremendous.
entries.reflection: Ayat al-Kursi says that neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Allah, and many Muslims recite it before sleep. When you cannot rest, He is still watching. If sleeplessness persists, speak to a medic or chaplain.
studyPrompts: What keeps you awake?
How could reciting this verse comfort you?
Who could help if you have not been sleeping?

entries.passageText: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful.
entries.reflection: The people of Medina loved those who came to them for refuge and preferred them above themselves, even in need. Welcoming strangers can be costly and beautiful.
studyPrompts: Who is new or far from home around you?
How could you welcome them?
When were you welcomed?

entries.passageText: He it is Who sent down peace of reassurance into the hearts of the believers that they might add faith unto their faith. Allah's are the hosts of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is ever Knower, Wise -
entries.reflection: Allah sends down tranquility, sakinah, into the hearts of believers so that they add faith to their faith. Calm is a gift that strengthens faith.
studyPrompts: When have you felt sudden calm?
What would you ask for under pressure?
How does calm help your faith?

entries.passageText: O ye who believe! Shun much suspicion; for lo! some suspicion is a crime. And spy not, neither backbite one another. Would one of you love to eat the flesh of his dead brother? Ye abhor that (so abhor the other)! And keep your duty (to Allah). Lo! Allah is Relenting, Merciful.
entries.reflection: Avoid much suspicion, do not spy, and do not backbite. The Qur'an compares backbiting to eating a dead brother's flesh. Gossip is serious.
studyPrompts: What suspicion are you carrying?
Have you spoken about someone behind their back?
How could you protect someone's reputation?

entries.passageText: He it is Who maketh you to go on the land and the sea till, when ye are in the ships and they sail with them with a fair breeze and they are glad therein, a storm-wind reacheth them and the wave cometh unto them from every side and they deem that they are overwhelmed therein; (then) they cry unto Allah, making their faith pure for Him only: If Thou deliver us from this, we truly will be of the thankful.
entries.reflection: When storm and waves overwhelm a ship, the people call on Allah with sincere faith. Storms reveal what we truly rely on.
studyPrompts: What storm are you in?
Whom do you call on?
How could you keep that sincerity after the storm?

entries.passageText: And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them,
entries.reflection: The believers conduct their affairs by mutual consultation, shura. Seeking and giving advice is part of faith.
studyPrompts: Whom do you consult?
What decision could use counsel?
How could you listen better?

entries.passageText: They said: Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost!
entries.reflection: Adam and his wife said, our Lord, we have wronged ourselves; if You do not forgive us we will be lost. Apology begins by admitting the wrong.
studyPrompts: What wrong do you need to admit?
Whom do you need to apologize to?
What stops you?

entries.passageText: And the sun runneth on unto a resting-place for him. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Wise. And for the moon We have appointed mansions till she return like an old shrivelled palm-leaf. It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor doth the night outstrip the day. They float each in an orbit.
entries.reflection: The sun runs its course and the moon has its phases; each floats in its orbit. The order of time and seasons is a sign.
studyPrompts: What season of life are you in?
What order do you see in creation?
How do changing seasons speak to you?

entries.passageText: Far removed from it will be the righteous Who giveth his wealth that he may grow (in goodness).
entries.reflection: The righteous give their wealth to grow in purity. Self-denial is about growing in goodness, not only giving things up.
studyPrompts: What could you give up for good?
How might it help you grow?
Whom could it benefit?

entries.passageText: Keep to forgiveness (O Muhammad), and enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant.
entries.reflection: Keep to forgiveness, enjoin kindness, and turn away from the ignorant. With difficult people, sometimes the wise choice is to step away.
studyPrompts: Who is difficult for you?
Where could you forgive?
When is it wise to turn away?

entries.passageText: On that day faces will be bright as dawn, Laughing, rejoicing at good news;
entries.reflection: On that day some faces will be bright as dawn, laughing and rejoicing. Hope for the end can brighten the face today.
studyPrompts: What brightens your face?
What are you hopeful about?
Whom could you cheer?

entries.passageText: So remember the name of thy Lord and devote thyself with a complete devotion -
entries.reflection: Remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him completely. Time alone in remembrance is a form of devotion.
studyPrompts: When do you have time alone?
How could you use it for remembrance?
What distracts you from devotion?

entries.passageText: If a woman feareth ill treatment from her husband, or desertion, it is no sin for them twain if they make terms of peace between themselves. Peace is better. But greed hath been made present in the minds (of men). If ye do good and keep from evil, lo! Allah is ever Informed of what ye do.
entries.reflection: Speaking of husband and wife, the Qur'an says: making peace is better. Reconciliation is better than prolonged conflict.
studyPrompts: What relationship needs peace?
What would making peace look like?
What gets in the way?

entries.passageText: Is not He (best) Who answereth the wronged one when he crieth unto Him and removeth the evil, and hath made you viceroys of the earth? Is there any Allah beside Allah? Little do they reflect!
entries.reflection: Who answers the distressed when they call and removes the evil? Allah hears those in danger and distress.
studyPrompts: What danger are you facing?
How could you call on Allah?
Whom could you pray for?

entries.passageText: And those who, when they are reminded of the revelations of their Lord, fall not deaf and blind thereat.
entries.reflection: The servants of the Beneficent do not fall deaf and blind when reminded. Receiving reminders with an open heart is a mark of faith.
studyPrompts: How do you receive reminders or criticism?
What reminder have you ignored?
How could you listen better?

entries.passageText: Then exalted be Allah, the True King! And hasten not (O Muhammad) with the Qur'an ere its revelation hath been perfected unto thee, and say: My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.
entries.reflection: My Lord, increase me in knowledge. This short prayer asks for more learning. Study is a form of worship.
studyPrompts: What are you learning?
What knowledge do you want?
How could you make study a habit?

entries.passageText: And of His portents (is this): that thou seest the earth lowly, but when We send down water thereon it thrilleth and groweth. Lo! He Who quickeneth it is verily the Quickener of the Dead. Lo! He is Able to do all things.
entries.reflection: When Allah sends rain on barren ground, it stirs and grows. Dry seasons can be followed by new life.
studyPrompts: Are you in a dry season?
What rain are you hoping for?
What new growth have you seen?

entries.passageText: For him are angels ranged before him and behind him, who guard him by Allah's command. Lo! Allah changeth not the condition of a folk until they (first) change that which is in their hearts; and if Allah willeth misfortune for a folk there is none that can repel it, nor have they a defender beside Him.
entries.reflection: Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. Change begins within.
studyPrompts: What change do you hope for?
What could you change in yourself?
What step could you take today?

entries.passageText: Or think ye that ye will enter paradise while yet there hath not come unto you the like of (that which came to) those who passed away before you? Affliction and adversity befell them, they were shaken as with earthquake, till the messenger (of Allah) and those who believed along with him said: When cometh Allah's help? Now surely Allah's help is nigh.
entries.reflection: Earlier believers faced affliction and were shaken until they asked when Allah's help would come, and Allah's help is near. Pain is shared by the faithful. Seek help, and trust that help is near.
studyPrompts: What pain are you facing?
Who has gone through similar pain?
Where could you find help now?

entries.passageText: And there may spring from you a nation who invite to goodness, and enjoin right conduct and forbid indecency. Such are they who are successful.
entries.reflection: Let there be among you a community that invites to good, enjoins right and forbids wrong. Community is built around shared goodness.
studyPrompts: Where is your community?
What good could you invite others to?
How could you strengthen it?

entries.passageText: Lo! those who go in awe for fear of their Lord. And those who believe in the revelations of their Lord,
entries.reflection: Those who are in awe of their Lord and believe in His signs are described with honor. Reverence is a posture of the heart.
studyPrompts: What fills you with awe?
How do you show reverence?
Where could you be more reverent?

entries.passageText: And We remove whatever rancour may be in their breasts. As brethren, face to face, (they rest) on couches raised.
entries.reflection: Allah will remove whatever rancor is in their hearts, and they will be brothers facing one another. Bitterness can be removed.
studyPrompts: What rancor is in your heart?
Who could you face as a brother or sister?
What would letting go look like?

entries.passageText: Call unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation, and reason with them in the better way. Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth from His way, and He is Best Aware of those who go aright.
entries.reflection: Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good counsel, and reason in the best way. Correction should be wise and kind.
studyPrompts: Who might you need to correct?
How could you do it wisely?
What would the best way look like?

entries.passageText: Establish worship at the going down of the sun until the dark of night, and (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn. Lo! (the recital of) the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed.
entries.reflection: Establish prayer from the decline of the sun to the darkness of night, and the recitation at dawn. The daily prayers give shape to every day.
studyPrompts: How do the daily prayers shape your day?
Which one is hardest to keep?
How could you protect your routine?

entries.passageText: And he turned away from them and said: Alas, my grief for Joseph! And his eyes were whitened with the sorrow that he was suppressing.
entries.reflection: Jacob turned away and said, alas, my grief for Joseph, and his eyes went white with sorrow. Even prophets grieved deeply.
studyPrompts: What sorrow are you carrying?
How does Jacob's grief speak to you?
Who could you share your sorrow with?

entries.passageText: And if ye go in fear, then (pray) standing or on horseback. And when ye are again in safety, remember Allah, as He hath taught you that which (heretofore) ye knew not.
entries.reflection: If you are in fear, pray on foot or riding; when safe again, remember Allah as He taught you. Worship adapts to circumstances.
studyPrompts: Where have you had to adapt your practice?
What stays the same?
How does this verse help when you are deployed?

entries.passageText: And He it is Who hath set for you the stars that ye may guide your course by them amid the darkness of the land and the sea. We have detailed Our revelations for a people who have knowledge.
entries.reflection: Allah made the stars to guide you through the darkness of land and sea. Navigators and night travelers have relied on them for ages.
studyPrompts: When did you last look at the stars?
What guides you in the dark?
How do the stars point to their Maker?

entries.passageText: Oh, but man is a telling witness against himself, Although he tender his excuses.
entries.reflection: Man is a witness against himself, even if he offers excuses. Conscience knows the truth.
studyPrompts: What does your conscience tell you?
What excuses do you make?
How could you listen to it?

entries.passageText: Lo! man was created anxious, Fretful when evil befalleth him And, when good befalleth him, grudging; Save worshippers.
entries.reflection: Man was created anxious, fretful when evil touches him, except those who pray. Prayer can lift us out of self-pity.
studyPrompts: When do you feel sorry for yourself?
How does prayer change it?
What could you do instead of fretting?

entries.passageText: Is the reward of goodness aught save goodness?
entries.reflection: Is the reward of goodness anything but goodness? Thanking those who are good to us is part of that.
studyPrompts: Who has been good to you?
How could you repay goodness?
Whom could you thank today?

entries.passageText: And We have commended unto man kindness toward parents. His mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance, and the bearing of him and the weaning of him is thirty months, till, when he attaineth full strength and reacheth forty years, he saith: My Lord! Arouse me that I may give thanks for the favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and that I may do right acceptable unto Thee. And be gracious unto me in the matter of my seed. Lo! I have turned unto Thee repentant, and lo! I am of those who surrender (unto Thee).
entries.reflection: At forty years a person prays to give thanks for Allah's favor on him and his parents, to do good, and for his children. Maturity brings gratitude and responsibility.
studyPrompts: What are you grateful for at this stage of life?
What do you want to do with your years?
Whom are you praying for?

entries.passageText: And say: Truth hath come and falsehood hath vanished away. Lo! falsehood is ever bound to vanish.
entries.reflection: Truth has come and falsehood has vanished; falsehood is bound to vanish. Truth lasts.
studyPrompts: What truth do you hold on to?
What falsehood do you need to let go?
How could you speak truth today?

entries.passageText: Such as remember Allah, standing, sitting, and reclining, and consider the creation of the heavens and the earth, (and say): Our Lord! Thou createdst not this in vain. Glory be to Thee! Preserve us from the doom of Fire.
entries.reflection: Those who remember Allah standing, sitting and lying down, and reflect on creation, say: You did not create this in vain. Purpose fills ordinary moments.
studyPrompts: When do you feel bored?
How could remembrance fill those moments?
Where do you see purpose?

entries.passageText: The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion (of right and wrong). And whosoever of you is present, let him fast the month, and whosoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast the same) number of other days. Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you; and (He desireth) that ye should complete the period, and that ye should magnify Allah for having guided you, and that peradventure ye may be thankful.
entries.reflection: The verse on Ramadan ends with a call to magnify Allah for guiding you and to be thankful. Eid celebrates the completion of the fast.
studyPrompts: What are you celebrating?
How could you give thanks?
How will you mark Eid where you are?

entries.passageText: Revile not those unto whom they pray beside Allah lest they wrongfully revile Allah through ignorance. Thus unto every nation have We made their deed seem fair. Then unto their Lord is their return, and He will tell them what they used to do.
entries.reflection: Do not revile those whom others call upon besides Allah. The Qur'an asks believers not to insult others' objects of worship.
studyPrompts: How do you speak about other faiths?
Where could you show more respect?
What does tolerance look like in a unit with many beliefs?

entries.passageText: And Job, when he cried unto his Lord, (saying): Lo! adversity afflicteth me, and Thou art Most Merciful of all who show mercy. Then We heard his prayer and removed that adversity from which he suffered, and We gave him his household (that he had lost) and the like thereof along with them, a mercy from Our store, and a remembrance for the worshippers;
entries.reflection: Job cried, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful. Allah heard him and removed his suffering. Crying out is the first step. If you are in despair, use Need to talk? in this app or speak to a chaplain today.
studyPrompts: What adversity is touching you?
Who could you talk to today?
What small thing still gives you hope?

entries.passageText: Be modest in thy bearing and subdue thy voice. Lo! the harshest of all voices is the voice of the ass.
entries.reflection: Luqman tells his son to be modest in bearing and lower his voice. Modesty shows in how we carry ourselves.
studyPrompts: How do you carry yourself?
When do you raise your voice?
What would modesty look like today?

entries.passageText: And when he turned his face toward Midian, he said: Peradventure my Lord will guide me in the right road.
entries.reflection: As Moses set out toward Midian, he said: perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right road. Departures can begin with hope for guidance.
studyPrompts: What departure are you facing?
What guidance do you need?
What hope do you carry?

entries.passageText: (And it was said unto him): O David! Lo! We have set thee as a viceroy in the earth; therefor judge aright between mankind, and follow not desire that it beguile thee from the way of Allah. Lo! those who wander from the way of Allah have an awful doom, forasmuch as they forgot the Day of Reckoning.
entries.reflection: Allah told David: We have made you a vicegerent, so judge rightly and do not follow desire. Power is a trust to be used justly.
studyPrompts: What authority do you have?
How do you use it?
Where could desire lead you astray?
